searchText: sorry for delay, merged now Can anyone confirm if `v1.5.0-alpha.3` spec test now correctly covers this change? https://github.com/ethereum/consensus-specs/pull/3769/ it seemed to for me -- until I fixed that, got a bunch of random-looking failures which that one fix mostly removed Interesting. I encounter several tests in `transition` where when calculating proposer index, some of the slots don't have a proposer index because this condition's never met: https://github.com/ethereum/consensus-specs/blob/00b74686e21af62e6498ee900f942f6f6689e294/specs/electra/beacon-chain.md?plain=1#L450 . Maybe it's my problem🤔 even if this loop is several iterations over the entire validator set it should find the solution eventually I see. That's the problem. Lodestar iterates the entire validator set only once to prevent an infinite loop. The tests passed when I allow it to iterate twice. Interesting that spec test previously didn't require us to loop more than once. With the previous spec the same validator balances were at the MaxEB which has changed since eip7251, i think it is important to test all clients with the increased MaxEB and not increased validator balances. The spec lacks tests where validator balances are below the MaxEB, before the MaxEB increase it was the edge case but now it becomes a common situation. I guess lodestar would fail to compute proposer index in the network where validators' EB is around 17 ETH and the set is small enough to make the loop iterate more than one time over the entire set Peerdas client update: <@476250636548308992> <@531934490826768418> is https://github.com/prysmaticlabs/prysm/tree/peerDAS still the active branch for peerdas? <@466006586477772831> <@688748669268132001> is https://github.com/sigp/lighthouse/tree/das still the active branch for peerdas? <@425907307621122049> <@720075860807254059> is master still the branch to use for teku? <@792822129019584562> <@578356786889752586> any lodestar branches to test peerdas with? <@654267572107083777> <@881905303011086387> any nimbus branches to test peerdas with? <@777935002263617576> any grandine branches to test peerdas with? excerpts.author: nc1234
excerpts.content: Can anyone confirm if `v1.5.0-alpha.3` spec test now correctly covers this change? https://github.com/ethereum/consensus-specs/pull/3769/

excerpts.author: tersec
excerpts.content: it seemed to for me -- until I fixed that, got a bunch of random-looking failures which that one fix mostly removed

excerpts.author: nc1234
excerpts.content: Interesting. I encounter several tests in `transition` where when calculating proposer index, some of the slots don't have a proposer index because this condition's never met: https://github.com/ethereum/consensus-specs/blob/00b74686e21af62e6498ee900f942f6f6689e294/specs/electra/beacon-chain.md?plain=1#L450 . Maybe it's my problem🤔

excerpts.author: m.kalinin
excerpts.content: even if this loop is several iterations over the entire validator set it should find the solution eventually

excerpts.author: nc1234
excerpts.content: I see. That's the problem. Lodestar iterates the entire validator set only once to prevent an infinite loop. The tests passed when I allow it to iterate twice. Interesting that spec test previously didn't require us to loop more than once.

excerpts.author: m.kalinin
excerpts.content: With the previous spec the same validator balances were at the MaxEB which has changed since eip7251, i think it is important to test all clients with the increased MaxEB and not increased validator balances. The spec lacks tests where validator balances are below the MaxEB, before the MaxEB increase it was the edge case but now it becomes a common situation. I guess lodestar would fail to compute proposer index in the network where validators' EB is around 17 ETH and the set is small enough to make the loop iterate more than one time over the entire set
